title: Motorola Signature 256GB for $468 Using $600 Bonus Trade-in Credit When Purchasing on 12 Month Plan @ Telstra
body:
Deal: Motorola Signature 256GB for $468 Using $600 Bonus Trade-in Credit When Purchasing on 12 Month Plan @ Telstra

[Armaghan] What are the eligible devices for trade in ?
[drillvoice] I've updated the post - you can check at https://www.telstra.com.au/trade-in
[shxhshzhz] Warning, YMMV . This Ozbargainer tried recently and commented this:
Thanks to the comment from Drillvoice above I tried using the Telstra deal instore but it is not quite as good as suggested.
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/comment/17859269/redir
From what I can see, the price match credit (with JB) of $200 is applied as credit to the Telstra account. So is the trade-in bonus and value. So if you have a use for $800 of credit on your Telstra account, then it comes down to an effective $400 cost, less the value of your trade. But if you would not choose to stay with Telstra until that credit gets used, not so great.
[AtomicHero] Under trade-in, it specifies the below:
If you receive a bill, your credit will appear by the second bill. Otherwise, you’ll receive it via your nominated payment method within 30 days.
I guess that's why OP says to make the bank account the default
[Dabbler68] That was my comment above suggesting the credit goes to Telstra Account. But I am happy to report that scouring through Telstra site, with the Upfront Mobile Plan the credit goes to the linked payment method.
Price match wording:
Credit will be applied within 2 billing cycles, or onto your bank account or credit or debit card, if you are on a Telstra Upfront Mobile Plan.
Trade-in credit wording (under FAQ):
Depending on the billing system, your credit will be applied by the second bill, or to your nominated credit/debit card within 30 days if you’re on an Upfront Mobile Plan.
[OZBsince2018] Thats why it is important to setup direct debit using a bank account. Doing so means, your credit will go to you bank account. Thats what happened to me and my trade in bonus was paid into my bank account
[jimojr] My trade in bonus was paid back to my credit card last time.
[OctoTheOctopo] This has got to be up there in terms of the most convoluted way to ozb your way to a discounted phone… upvoted just for the chaos
[Jd0911] Don’t Telstra give you the original discounted device price spread across the months of your plan? And cancelling it early voids the monthly discount off the phones RRP, which in turn you would have to pay out the full price of the phone? Or am I overthinking it?
[AtomicHero] I know Optus voids the discount but Telstra says:
"Device discounts still apply to cancelled orders bought on repayment"
[Jd0911] No, if you cancel your Telstra plan early, you typically lose any ongoing promotional credits or bill credits tied to a handset discount, and you must pay out the remaining device balance based on the full standard undiscounted price.
What Happens When You Cancel
Remaining Repayments: You must pay the balance of your remaining device payment contract (DPC) in one final lump-sum payment on your closing bill.
Loss of Credits/Discounts: Any promotional monthly bill credits or conditional handset discounts that were meant to offset the cost of the phone over 12, 24, or 36 months are usually forfeited upon cancellation.
Payout Calculation: The final payout amount defaults to the remaining undiscounted value of the hardware.
[AtomicHero] Perhaps but the associated mobile plan is month to month and not a locked in contract. The mobile service plan says "cancel anytime".
In terms of the DPC (on the Motorola signature page) it says:
Device Payment Contract (DPC)
You must have an eligible Telstra Mobile Plan in order to have a DPC. If you cancel your DPC early, cancel your mobile plan during the device payment term or move to an ineligible mobile plan during the payment term, you’ll need to pay out your device, in full. Device discounts still apply to cancelled orders bought on repayment.
Obviously I could be wrong but I intend to stop by Telstra tomorrow and ask some questions.
[OZBsince2018] No. Read the OPs post again. All steps are correctly mentioned and I can confim all worked for me.
[Jd0911] Have you received a final payout bill with the discounted price still applied ?
[OZBsince2018] Yes. My remaining monthly device instalment payments reflected the discounted price after the price match was approved. So when I cancelled the plan, received an invoice from Telstra for the remaining device payment based on discounted device cost.
[Duece1995] Need to do a credit check. It says minimum cost is $1986 odd. What an i missing?
[AtomicHero] I have 2 questions which I haven't been able to locate across comments / T&C
Even if the Telstra account was credited with the price match + trade-in credit, could you not use that credit to pay off the remainder of the phone after cancelling the service?
If booking the trade-in with Telstra, do they asses the phone and release the funds then and there? Or does it get sent to the 3rd party assessor and you need to wait?
[OZBsince2018] You can take the trade in device to a Telstra store and they will asses and process the trade in there and there, but trade in value will hit your bank account in a a few days.
[AtomicHero] Thanks mate.
Do you know what tests they run / how long it takes? More so if I decide to go during business hours.
[OZBsince2018] Nothing as such. Just physical inspection etc
[OZBsince2018] I can as I received the trade in credit and bonus in my bank account setup as direct debit.
[PLA74] Wonder if it works on a iPhone 17 Pro Max 512GB?
[Usemame] I feel like this is the phone version of this deal
[HitlersDad] This sounds like a gamble. If someone does it post back here my good fellows.
[Dabbler68] Simplifying for those that find it too hard …. still get it for $468.
Sign up for the Upfront Mobile Plan and pay first month ($74 or $69 with "Promo" code). Cancel without penalty at any time. You must be on this plan for it all to work. The wording (I posted above) says it works with credit card.
Buy the phone outright for $1,199.
Submit a price match request (JB Hifi $999) = $200 to your bank account/card.
Submit a trade-in request with elligible phone. Drop your old phone into a store or send via Aust Post for free. = $600 to your bank account/card + value of trade-in. The phone will get validated to ensure it works fine.
Or go to a store and watch someone else do it all.
Cost $1,199 + $69
Credit to bank $800 + value of phone.
[OZBsince2018] I can confirm all above worked for me when I originally commented about this deal. Not that complicated as it seems. But great result in the end.
[OhNoUShiz] Sorry am confused. Did you trade in your phone purchased in step 1?
Any phones to get the $600?
[AtomicHero] Thanks Dabbler68.
I'll follow this and pay outright, submit price match / trade-in and then cancel plan within the month. I think it's simpler.
For those wondering about JB price match. The phone is in the "Deals for Dad" catalogue on page 29 and ends on the 7th
https://catalogue.jbhifi.com.au/2026/08/27-08-fd3/29/index.h…
[OzSikh] So after signing up for the $74/69 plan, you can actually buy the phone outright? The instructions in the OP say it needs to be bought on a 12/24/36 months plan.
[Kenji777] I did exactly the same process today instore using a debit card, will send the trade in phone tomorrow. Hope they send the bonus and price match difference in the bank card.
[OhNoUShiz] So the $600 trade in is given no matter the type of phone to trade in as long as it is working fine?
[djkelly69] Buy the motorola signature and successfully complete a trade-in request by 7 September to get $600 bonus credit on top of the value of your old device.
(emphasis added)
The $600 is a bonus in addition to whatever they give you for the device you are trading in.
[Kenji777] As long as their system accepts it, no matter the value of the phone, the $600 bonus should be paid. The trade in credit+bonus will be paid only after their trade in partner receives and assess the device. There is certain risk in this process, cause the trade in bonus and price match are all after sale, so you have to pay $1199 upfront and wait couple of weeks to get the bonus credit back. And I think they don't do change of mind returns. I took the risk today, now it’s the waiting game. Just hoping they will send the credit in the bank card.
[HT10] Did the same today in store. Got $10 off the $74 plan and did the trade-in on the spot. They’ve got little booths there so you can sit down and transfer everything across.
Once I was done, I reset the old phone, handed it over and walked out. About 5 mins later I got a notification confirming the $600 trade-in credit, plus my phone’s trade-in value refunded back to my card, with a PDF receipt showing in the Telstra app.
[Kenji777] The store agent told me its quicker if i post my device myself through auspost, cuz they send all the phone to their tradein partner on wednesday. Where are you located?
I thought the trade in bonus is credited only after their trade in partner (assurant) receive the device.
[Kenji777] Did you pay using bank card? And were you able to price match?
[xrailgun] Sorry if this is obvious, but I just wanted to double check.
For TRS purposes, is the invoice for the phone itself actually showing the full $1,199?
[jimbobinator] Telstra will give you $540 for trading in the Motorola Signature.
Keep the mobile service active and pay out the device, each time you do this you make $141 profit.
[yummypinacolada] That is such a loophole, how many times can you do before your Telstra account is banned though.

I have a Huawei P30 Pro (which is somehow still on the trade-in list) that has a lightly cracked screen but otherwise usable, so would be happy to trade it in and get ~$0 for it plus the $600 bonus rather than trade in a newer phone.
Any chance this would work?
[jimojr] No, the trade in value needs to be at least $1 to qualify.
[High] When they match the price, do they take into account the monthly discount for the long term plan?
Otherwise it should be a $200 discount to $999 for the price match and another $100 discount if staying 12 months.
